answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded identity: before an agent can transact, it must lock a refundable economic stake, so spawning a swarm of fakes costs real capital. The bond acts like a ferrous anchor, weighing down cheap clones, while a slashing rule prunes misbehavior the way a gardener clears invasive yarrow. Reputation then glows like a lantern, guiding counterparties toward staked, accountable peers instead of free throwaway identities.
